concepts.title: CIA Triad, Threat, Vulnerability และ Risk: คิดแบบผู้ป้องกัน
concepts.covers: Matches Part 1 Steps 1-2. Open with a Security callout (ethics and law: own lab or legal platforms only, พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์). CIA triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability) with one attack example each (data leak, tampered price, DDoS); Threat vs Vulnerability vs Risk vs Exploit; Risk = Likelihood x Impact (both 1-5, score 1-25; Low 1-6, Medium 7-14, High 15-19, Critical 20-25); Defense in Depth, Least Privilege, Zero Trust; AAA. Runnable example: ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c01/risk_score.py (stdlib only) that reads assets.csv (the 5 sample assets in notes) and prints a table sorted by risk score with level labels and which CIA side is hit; also prints a count per level. Mistakes: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'assets.csv' (wrong working directory), ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10 (header row or blank line in CSV), confusing Threat with Vulnerability in the asset sheet.

concepts.title: เข้าใจผู้โจมตีเพื่อป้องกัน: Cyber Kill Chain และ MITRE ATT&CK
concepts.covers: Matches Step 3, defender view only (no attack instructions). The 7 Lockheed Martin Kill Chain phases (Reconnaissance, Weaponization, Delivery, Exploitation, Installation, Command and Control, Actions on Objectives) and where a defender can break each; MITRE ATT&CK structure: Tactic (why) -> Technique (how) -> Sub-technique, IDs like TA0006 Credential Access, T1110 Brute Force, T1110.001 Password Guessing, T1078 Valid Accounts, T1046 Network Service Discovery, T1021.004 Remote Services: SSH, T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application, T1566 Phishing; tell learners to verify IDs at attack.mitre.org because the framework is updated. Runnable example: ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c02/map_incident.py that loads a synthetic incident timeline incident_events.json (6 events from the shared scenario in notes: nmap-style scan from 203.0.113.45, many failed SSH logins, one successful login, new user created, outbound connection) and prints each event with its Kill Chain phase, ATT&CK technique ID and a recommended detection/mitigation, then a coverage summary. Mistakes: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter (broken JSON), KeyError: 'technique' (missing field), mapping a technique to the wrong tactic.

concepts.title: Hashing และ Integrity: sha256sum, hashlib และทำไมต้องมี Salt
concepts.covers: Matches Step 4 (first half). Hash properties (one-way, fixed length, avalanche effect, collision resistance), MD5/SHA-1 are broken for security, SHA-256 for integrity; verify a downloaded file with sha256sum -c; hash vs encryption vs encoding (base64 is NOT security). Runnable examples: (1) bash: create ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c03/report.txt, sha256sum it, write SHA256SUMS, sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS -> 'report.txt: OK', modify one character and re-check -> 'report.txt: FAILED' plus 'sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match'; (2) hash_demo.py with hashlib.sha256 showing avalanche effect between 'somchai' and 'Somchai', identical unsalted hashes for two users with the same password 'password123', and different hashes once a random salt from secrets.token_hex(16) is added; hashlib.file_digest for a file (3.11+). Explain why fast hashes (even salted) are still wrong for passwords -> c07. Mistakes: TypeError: Strings must be encoded before hashing, comparing hashes with different case/whitespace, trusting a checksum downloaded from the same compromised page.

concepts.title: Symmetric vs Asymmetric Encryption, Digital Signature และ TLS Certificate ด้วย openssl
concepts.covers: Matches Step 4 (second half). Symmetric (AES-256, one shared key, fast) vs asymmetric (RSA, Ed25519 key pair; encrypt with public, sign with private); key exchange idea; digital signatures; TLS handshake overview, CA, chain of trust, self-signed certs only for labs. Runnable bash example in ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c04 with OpenSSL 3.0.13: openssl rand -hex 32; openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 -salt -in secret.txt -out secret.enc -pass pass:LabOnly-ChangeMe then decrypt (note: -pass on the command line only for the lab, real work uses a prompt or key file); openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out signer.key, openssl pkey -pubout, openssl pkeyutl -sign/-verify -rawin with 'Signature Verified Successfully' and failure after tampering; openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:3072 -nodes -days 30 -subj '/CN=localhost' -addext 'subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1'; openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName; openssl s_server -accept 127.0.0.1:8443 and openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:8443 -servername localhost -brief showing Protocol version: TLSv1.3 and 'Verification error: self-signed certificate'. Mistakes: 'bad decrypt' (wrong password or missing -pbkdf2 on decrypt), 'Could not open file or uri for loading private key', confusing which key signs vs verifies.

concepts.title: Linux Hardening: Users, sudo, File Permissions และ SSH Hardening
concepts.covers: Matches Step 5. Accounts (adduser, usermod -aG sudo, passwd -l, /etc/passwd vs /etc/shadow perms), sudo and visudo, least privilege; chmod/chown, octal modes 600/640/644/700/750, umask 027, SUID/SGID awareness (find / -perm -4000 -type f to INVENTORY only, compare with a baseline), world-writable files. SSH hardening via drop-in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-hardening.conf (PermitRootLogin no, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes, MaxAuthTries 3, LoginGraceTime 30, AllowUsers somchai, X11Forwarding no, ClientAliveInterval 300, ClientAliveCountMax 2), ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'somchai@lab', validate with sudo sshd -t and sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei 'permitrootlogin|passwordauthentication|maxauthtries', reload with sudo systemctl reload ssh (Ubuntu 24.04 uses ssh.socket activation; mention). Always keep a second session open before reloading. Lynis 3.0.9: sudo lynis audit system --quick and reading Hardening index. Runnable example: ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c05/perm_audit.sh (bash, read-only checks) that reports: files in a target folder with mode looser than expected, world-writable files, private keys not 600, and lists SUID binaries vs a saved baseline; run against a prepared demo folder lab-home/ with deliberately loose files, show output, then fix with chmod and re-run showing all PASS. Mistakes: 'Bad owner or permissions on /home/somchai/.ssh/config', 'sshd: no hostkeys available -- exiting' / '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-hardening.conf line 3: Bad configuration option', locking yourself out after PasswordAuthentication no without a working key.

concepts.title: Firewall, fail2ban และ Patch อัตโนมัติ (รวม Windows Defender และ Windows Firewall)
concepts.covers: Matches Step 6. ufw 0.36.2: default deny incoming / allow outgoing, ufw limit 22/tcp, allow from 192.0.2.0/24 to any port 22 proto tcp, ufw status verbose / numbered, delete rule; note WSL2 networking caveats (ufw inside WSL protects the WSL VM, Windows Firewall protects the host). fail2ban 1.0.2: /etc/fail2ban/jail.local with [sshd] enabled = true, backend = systemd, maxretry = 5, findtime = 10m, bantime = 1h, ignoreip = 127.0.0.1/8 ::1; fail2ban-client status sshd; runnable offline check: fail2ban-regex against the shared sample auth.log (sample/auth.log, see notes) with filter sshd showing matched lines count. unattended-upgrades 2.9.1: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades, sudo unattended-upgrade --dry-run --debug. Windows counterpart (env win, PowerShell 5.1/7, run as Administrator, not run in sandbox, official syntax): Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated; Update-MpSignature; Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name,Enabled,DefaultInboundAction. Mistakes: 'ERROR: Couldn't determine iptables version' or ufw not active in WSL, fail2ban 'ERROR  Failed during configuration: ... have no section', locking out your own IP (use ignoreip), PowerShell 'Access is denied' when not elevated.

concepts.title: Authentication: Password Hashing ด้วย Argon2/bcrypt, MFA (TOTP) และ Passkeys
concepts.covers: Matches Step 7. Why sha256(password) is wrong (fast = cheap to guess offline); Argon2id (recommended, argon2-cffi 25.1.0 PasswordHasher defaults, encoded string $argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$...), bcrypt 5.0.0 (cost 12, 72-byte limit: bcrypt 5 raises ValueError for longer passwords), check_needs_rehash; constant-time comparison with hmac.compare_digest; MFA factors (know/have/are), TOTP RFC 6238 with pyotp 2.10.0 (random_base32, now(), verify with valid_window=1, provisioning_uri for an authenticator app, issuer 'SecLab'); password managers; passkeys (WebAuthn/FIDO2: private key stays on device, phishing-resistant) concept only; RBAC vs ABAC tiny dict-based check. Runnable example: ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c07/auth_demo.py in a venv (pip install argon2-cffi==25.1.0 bcrypt==5.0.0 pyotp==2.10.0): register somchai and malee in an in-memory dict with Argon2id, verify correct/wrong password (VerifyMismatchError caught), time 1 Argon2 hash vs 100000 sha256 to show cost, bcrypt hash/checkpw, TOTP generate + verify (outputs that vary like hashes/codes must be described as machine-specific), RBAC can(user, action). Mistakes: argon2.exceptions.VerifyMismatchError uncaught, TypeError: Unicode-objects must be encoded before hashing / bcrypt expects bytes, TOTP always invalid because system clock is wrong (WSL clock drift: sudo hwclock -s).

concepts.title: Network Security ในแล็บตัวเอง: nmap, tcpdump บน Loopback และ IDS/IPS
concepts.covers: Matches Step 8. Security callout: scan ONLY 127.0.0.1 or your own containers; scanning others without permission is illegal. Ports/services review, TCP 3-way handshake, attack surface = listening services; ss -tlnp to list listeners first. Start two local services: python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 and the c04 openssl s_server on 127.0.0.1:8443. nmap 7.94: nmap -sT -p 1-10000 127.0.0.1, nmap -sV -p 8000,8443 127.0.0.1, -oN ~/projects/sec-lab/scans/nmap-localhost.txt; read states open/closed/filtered. tcpdump 4.99.4: sudo tcpdump -i lo -nn -A 'tcp port 8000' -c 12 while curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/ shows readable HTTP (GET / HTTP/1.1, User-Agent: curl/8.5.0), then the same on 8443 shows only encrypted bytes; save with -w lab.pcap and read with -r. IDS vs IPS, signature vs anomaly detection, network vs host-based (Suricata, Snort, Zeek, Wazuh named as concepts only), segmentation and firewalls. Runnable example: ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c08/diff_scans.py that parses two nmap -oG grepable files (before/after stopping the 8000 service) and reports newly opened/closed ports — the change-detection idea used in the Mini Project. Mistakes: 'tcpdump: lo: You don't have permission to capture on that device' (needs sudo), nmap showing 'All 1000 scanned ports on localhost (127.0.0.1) are in ignored states' because service was bound elsewhere/not started, 'Failed to resolve' typo in target.

concepts.title: Web Security 1: OWASP Top 10 และการป้องกัน SQL Injection ด้วย Parameterized Query
concepts.covers: Matches Step 9 (part 1). OWASP Top 10 overview (the 2025 edition named in Part 1; tell learners to confirm the current list at owasp.org/Top10 before citing it). Security callout: own lab on 127.0.0.1 only. Defensive focus: explain conceptually why building SQL by string concatenation lets input change the query's meaning, using the textbook single-quote example only as a short illustration; the page must center on the FIX. Runnable example in ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c09/ with Flask 3.1.3 + stdlib sqlite3: init_db.py creates shop.db (sample data in notes); app.py exposes GET /products?name=... implemented with a parameterized query (cursor.execute('SELECT ... WHERE name = ?', (name,))) and input length validation; test_app.py (pytest 9.1.1 + Flask test_client) proves that input containing quotes is treated as plain data (returns 0 rows, no error) and that a normal search works. Also show the safe-coding checklist: parameterized queries / ORM, least-privilege DB account, generic error messages (no stack traces to users, debug=False), input validation as a second layer. Mistakes: sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: products (forgot init_db.py), sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Incorrect number of bindings supplied (passing a string instead of a 1-tuple), running Flask with debug=True and exposing the Werkzeug debugger.

concepts.title: Web Security 2: Output Encoding กัน XSS, CSRF, Secure Headers และ Secrets Management
concepts.covers: Matches Step 9 (part 2). Concept of XSS (untrusted input rendered as HTML) explained without payload walkthroughs; the defence: Jinja2 autoescape (never mark user input |safe), markupsafe.escape, Content-Security-Policy. CSRF concept and defence (CSRF token, SameSite=Lax cookies, Flask session cookie flags SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY/SECURE/SAMESITE). Secure headers added in an @app.after_request hook: Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'", X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, X-Frame-Options DENY, Strict-Transport-Security (only meaningful over HTTPS). Secrets: SECRET_KEY read from environment / .env (python-dotenv 1.2.1), .env in .gitignore, .env.example committed, generate with python3 -c 'import secrets;print(secrets.token_hex(32))'. Runnable example ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c10/: app.py with GET /hello?name=... rendered via render_template_string with autoescape, plus test_app.py that asserts angle brackets in input come back escaped (<) and that all security headers are present; also curl -i http://127.0.0.1:5000/hello?name=somchai showing real headers. Mistakes: RuntimeError: The session is unavailable because no secret key was set, a .env file accidentally committed (git rm --cached .env and rotate the secret), CSP blocking your own inline script (move JS to a static file).

concepts.title: Logging, Monitoring และ Detection: วิเคราะห์ auth.log ด้วย Python และพื้นฐาน SOC
concepts.covers: Matches Step 10. Where logs live on Ubuntu 24.04 (/var/log/auth.log via rsyslog, journalctl -u ssh --since '1 hour ago', journalctl _COMM=sshd -o short-iso); Ubuntu 24.04 rsyslog writes RFC 3339 timestamps (2026-10-20T02:14:07.512345+07:00), older systems write 'Oct 20 02:14:07'. Defender-side detection only: synthetic sample/auth.log (see notes) — never a password-guessing tool. Runnable example ~/projects/sec-lab/code/c11/ssh_detector.py (stdlib: re, collections, datetime, argparse, json): parse 'Failed password', 'Invalid user', 'Accepted publickey|password' lines; alert when one IP has >= 5 failures within 10 minutes (sliding window), and raise severity HIGH when that IP later logs in successfully; print a summary table and write alerts.json; --threshold and --window flags. SOC basics: SIEM concepts (collection, normalization, correlation, dashboards; Wazuh, Splunk, Elastic named), alert triage, True/False Positive, severity, escalation. Windows counterpart (env win, run as Administrator, not run in sandbox): Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4625} -MaxEvents 10 (4625 failed logon, 4624 success, 4720 user created) and Event Viewer path. Mistakes: PermissionError reading /var/log/auth.log (use sudo or the adm group), regex not matching the RFC 3339 timestamp format, timezone-naive vs aware datetime TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes.

concepts.title: Vulnerability Management, Threat Modeling (STRIDE) และ Incident Response (NIST)
concepts.covers: Matches Steps 11-12. CVE, CWE, CVSS v3.1/v4.0 severity bands (None 0, Low 0.1-3.9, Medium 4.0-6.9, High 7.0-8.9, Critical 9.0-10.0), patch prioritization (CVSS + exposure + exploitation known, e.g. CISA KEV), SBOM idea. Runnable: in a venv, requirements-old.txt pinning flask==2.2.0 then pip-audit 2.10.1 -r requirements-old.txt showing the known Flask advisory (paste the real output, IDs as printed), upgrade to flask==3.1.3 and re-run to 'No known vulnerabilities found'; npm audit mentioned for Node. STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege) applied to the c09/c10 Flask app with a simple data flow (Browser -> Flask -> SQLite) and a threat table with mitigations; a small stride_table.py printing that table as Markdown for the report. Incident Response per NIST SP 800-61 (Preparation; Detection & Analysis; Containment, Eradication & Recovery; Post-Incident Activity; mention Rev. 3 aligns IR with CSF 2.0), evidence handling and chain of custody basics, writing an incident timeline from the c11 alerts. Mistakes: pip-audit 'ERROR: ... externally-managed-environment' (no venv), treating CVSS as the only priority signal, fixing before preserving evidence.

mini_project.name: Home Lab Security Assessment
mini_project.summary: A documented security assessment of the learner's OWN lab in ~/projects/home-lab-assessment: harden an Ubuntu 24.04 machine (WSL or a local container), scan it from localhost with nmap before and after hardening, run OWASP Juice Shop in Docker bound to 127.0.0.1:3000 and record findings mapped to the OWASP Top 10, write a Python log analyzer that detects SSH brute-force patterns in a synthetic auth.log, and write a professional findings report. Defensive, own-lab only.
features: hardening/: 99-hardening.conf (sshd drop-in), jail.local (fail2ban), ufw-rules.sh, harden.sh (users/sudo/permissions/unattended-upgrades), validated with sshd -t and lynis audit system --quick (Hardening index before/after)
scans/: nmap-before.txt and nmap-after.txt from nmap -sT -sV against 127.0.0.1 only, plus diff_scans.py comparing them

webapp/: docker run -d --name juice-shop -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 bkimminich/juice-shop (pin the tag you used and record its digest); findings.md mapping observed issues to OWASP Top 10 categories without exploit walkthroughs
detector/: log_analyzer.py (threshold 5 failures / 10 minutes per IP, HIGH when followed by a success, JSON + Markdown output), sample/auth.log, tests/test_log_analyzer.py (pytest, at least 5 tests)
deps/: pip-audit report of the detector's requirements

report/findings-report.md: Executive Summary, Scope and Rules of Engagement (own lab, date, author somchai), Methodology, Findings table (ID, title, severity by CVSS band, evidence, recommendation, status), Timeline, Lessons learned
README.md with how to reproduce, plus GitHub push
mini_project.stack: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (WSL2), Python 3.12.3 venv, pytest==9.1.1, pip-audit==2.10.1, OpenSSH 9.6p1, ufw 0.36.2, fail2ban 1.0.2, unattended-upgrades 2.9.1, Lynis 3.0.9, nmap 7.94, tcpdump 4.99.4, OpenSSL 3.0.13, Docker Desktop 4.95.0 (WSL 2 backend) with bkimminich/juice-shop, Git 2.43.0 + GitHub

versions.powershell: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7, run as Administrator (not runnable in sandbox)

notes: SAFETY SCOPE (mandatory for Parts 2-4): defensive, own-lab curriculum. Every attack topic is explained conceptually and paired with its fix or detection on the learner's own 127.0.0.1 lab. No exploit code, attack payload walkthroughs, brute-force or password-guessing tools, malware, persistence, privilege escalation, evasion, phishing material, or scanning of hosts the learner does not own. For hands-on offensive practice, point to TryHackMe, Hack The Box, OverTheWire Bandit and picoCTF. Put a Security callout (ethics + พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์) at the start of Part 2 and near c08, c09, c10.

Username somchai, home /home/somchai. Lab root ~/projects/sec-lab with notes/, scans/, logs/, reports/ (from Part 1) and code/cNN/ for each concept. Mini Project lives in ~/projects/home-lab-assessment.

Ports: Flask demo 127.0.0.1:5000, python http.server 127.0.0.1:8000, openssl s_server 127.0.0.1:8443, Juice Shop 127.0.0.1:3000, DVWA 127.0.0.1:8080. Always bind with 127.0.0.1 (docker -p 127.0.0.1:HOST:CONTAINER).
IPs: only 127.0.0.1 and documentation ranges. Suspicious sources 203.0.113.45 and 198.51.100.23; trusted admin network 192.0.2.0/24 with somchai's laptop 192.0.2.10. Lab hostname lab-ubuntu.
Sample assets.csv (c01) columns name,cia,likelihood,impact: laptop-somchai,C,3,4; ssh-server,CIA,4,5; customer-db,C,3,5; backup-drive,A,2,4; company-website,IA,4,3.

Incident scenario (c02, c11, c12, report): on 2026-10-20 from 02:10 to 02:40 +07:00, 203.0.113.45 probes ports, then generates many SSH 'Failed password'/'Invalid user' lines against users admin, root, test, then one 'Accepted password for test' at 02:31, then a new local user 'backup2' is created and an outbound connection to 198.51.100.23:4444 is seen. Legit activity: somchai logs in with publickey from 192.0.2.10. 198.51.100.23 has 3 failures only (below threshold).

sample/auth.log: synthetic, RFC 3339 timestamps like '2026-10-20T02:14:07.512345+07:00 lab-ubuntu sshd[2211]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 203.0.113.45 port 51234 ssh2'; around 30-40 lines; same file reused by c06 (fail2ban-regex), c11 and the Mini Project. Detector must also accept the classic 'Oct 20 02:14:07' format.

Flask demo DB shop.db: users(id, username, password_hash, role) with somchai/admin role 'admin', malee/'member', and products(id, name, price) with 3 rows: 'Notebook' 25000, 'Mouse' 590, 'Keyboard' 1290. password_hash values are Argon2id strings, never plaintext.

Terminology: keep English terms (Hardening, Firewall, Hash, Salt, Detection, Alert, Triage, Finding) in Thai sentences; Blue Team/Red Team/Purple Team/GRC; refer to the law as พ.ร.บ.ว่าด้วยการกระทำความผิดเกี่ยวกับคอมพิวเตอร์ (พ.ร.บ.คอมพิวเตอร์).
Outputs that vary per machine (hashes, salts, TOTP codes, PIDs, timestamps, ports from ephemeral range) must be labelled in Thai as values that will differ on the learner's machine.
Certifications (spec section 2): ISC2 CC, CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 (SY0-801 ~2026-11-17), CySA+ CS0-004, eJPT, OSCP+.
